title: Gyoza (Japanese Potstickers)
description: Gyoza are Japanese pan-fried dumplings with a juicy pork-and-cabbage filling and a golden, crispy bottom. Serve them with a simple homemade soy-vinegar dipping sauce.
notes: Salting draws out the moisture so the wrappers don't get soggy. Alternatively, you can blanch or microwave the thick, hard leaves until soft, or skip wilting altogether. Kneading binds the meat proteins so the texture is springy and smooth. The gyoza skin edges dry out quickly. Covering with a damp kitchen cloth or paper towel keeps them moist and easy to use. Do not overstuff the gyoza or the filling will squeeze out and make folding difficult. Cook the gyoza in batches or use two frying pans. You can also arrange them in one or two rows if preferred, leaving space between each piece. Steam frozen gyoza an extra 1–2 minutes. Because you flash froze the gyoza, they won't stick to each other in the bag. Shape leftover filling into mini meatballs or patties and pan-fry until cooked through. Cool, pack in an airtight container, and store in the fridge for up to 3 days or in the freezer for up to a month. Fill leftover wrappers with sliced cheese, fold and press to seal, and pan-fry until golden on both sides. They are a favorite with kids! For a different folding style, see How to Fold Gyoza: https: //www.justonecookbook.com/how-to-fold-gyoza/. Vegetable Gyoza recipe: https: //www.justonecookbook.com/vegetable-gyoza/. Homemade Gyoza Wrappers: https: //www.justonecookbook.com/gyoza-wrappers/. Homemade La-yu: https: //www.justonecookbook.com/homemade-la-yu/.

ingredients.name: gyoza wrappers (52 sheets per package; you can make homemade Gyoza Wrappers)
ingredients.raw: 1 package gyoza wrappers (52 sheets per package (10 oz, 284 g); you can make homemade Gyoza Wrappers)

steps.text: Prepare a small bowl of water and a baking sheet lined with parchment paper or dusted with 2 Tbsp potato starch (or cornstarch).
Open {i12} and cover them with a damp towel or plastic wrap at all times.

Hold one wrapper in the palm of your non-dominant hand (left hand for me). Measure 1 level Tbsp (or a scant 3/4 Tbsp for beginners) of filling with a small cookie scoop. Place the filling in the center of the wrapper and flatten it with the scooper bowl to press out any trapped air.
Dip one finger in {i13} and use it to moisten a circle on the wrapper's outer 1/4 inch (6 mm).
Fold the wrapper in half over the filling. Pinch the two sides together at the top center, but don't seal it yet.

Right side: Starting to the right of top center, fold a pleat leaning toward the center into the top half of the wrapper using your right thumb and index finger. Tightly press the folded pleat against the back half of the wrapper using your left thumb and index finger. Fold 2–3 more pleats on the right side 1/4 inch (6 mm) apart. Press to seal any gaps.

Left side: To the left of top center, fold a pleat leaning toward the center into the top half of the wrapper using your left thumb and index finger. Tightly press the folded pleat against the back half of the wrapper using your right thumb and index finger. Fold 2–3 more pleats along the left side every 1/4 inch (6 mm). Press one last time to seal any gaps and secure the pleats.

Evenly distribute the filling and make the bottom flat so the gyoza sits upright. Place on the baking sheet and cover with plastic wrap to avoid drying. Fold the remaining gyoza. Cook or freeze the folded dumplings right away before the filling releases moisture and makes {i12} soggy.
Heat a large nonstick or carbon steel frying pan over medium heat. When hot, add {i14}.
Dust off any potato starch from the gyoza bottoms with a pastry brush.

Place the gyoza in the pan, flat side down in a single layer in a circular pattern. Leave space between each piece so they don't touch. Cook about 3 minutes, until the bottoms are golden brown and release cleanly from the pan.
Add {i16} to the pan and immediately cover with a lid. Steam for about 3 minutes, until most of the water evaporates.
Remove the lid and cook until {i16} fully evaporates, about 1 minute.
Drizzle {i15} around the gyoza and cook, uncovered, until the bottoms are deep golden and crisp.
